acceptance: .github/theseus-lock.json pins a Theseus release that contains the theseus#77 fix
A listed attester comment on #2807 passes is_attested_review and the digest closes the issue
context: Filed after the external reviews of the seven open soundness gap issues on 2026-11-12: six closed clean, #2807 kept its Medium finding.
description:
## Problem
Soundness gap issue BenchBox-dev/benchbox#2807 (commit 9c005a17a, PR #2769) stays open on one live Medium finding. The external review posted on the issue traced the retarget timing race from the pre-extraction oracle into the pinned Theseus package: theseus_reviewer/github.py:292-299 (_pull_request_target_trusted) trusts a pull_request_target run's state artifact when the pull request's last base change precedes run.created_at, without proof of which branch's workflow ran. The run path carries no source ref. The fix is tracked upstream as joeharris76/theseus#77. The owner chose to track it there rather than fix it now.

## Change
After a Theseus release contains the fix for #77, promote .github/theseus-lock.json to that release through the normal lock-bump flow. Then run an external review (codex, muse or agy) of the fixed trust check and the #2807 threads, and have a listed attester post the clean result on #2807 so the soundness digest closes it.

## Guardrails
- Do not post an attestation while the race is still present in the pinned version.
- An alternative is an owner decision to accept the race explicitly; that is the owner's call, not an agent's.
